text: Permitting his pupil himself to taste things, and of himself to discern and choose them, sometimes opening the way to him, and sometimes leaving him to open it for himself; that is, I would not have him alone to invent and speak, but that he should also hear his pupil speak in turn.
author: Michel de Montaigne
locator: Book I, Chapter 25, Of the Education of Children
translation: Charles Cotton, ed. W. C. Hazlitt, 1877
